stories.headline: Adonai Mitchell had surgical procedure on finger, expected to miss Week 6
stories.summary: Jets receiver Adonai Mitchell underwent a surgical procedure last month on his injured finger and is expected to miss a fourth consecutive game Sunday.
stories.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- When Adonai Mitchell injured a finger in practice before Week 3, the New York Jets decided not to put the wide receiver on injured reserve, thinking he'd be back within four weeks.

As it turned out, Mitchell underwent surgery about a week later, coach Aaron Glenn revealed Wednesday, and now is expected to miss his fourth consecutive game.

Mitchell is still considered week-to-week, according to Glenn. It means Tim Patrick, who returned last week from a four-week stint on IR, likely will start alongside Garrett Wilson when the Jets (2-3) face the New England Patriots (3-2) on Sunday at Gillette Stadium.

Rookie Omar Cooper Jr., who has missed four games with a high ankle sprain, also could be a factor as he was designated to return from IR.

Mitchell's injury has been a mystery. Glenn has been evasive, claiming last week that he didn't know if the finger was fractured or sprained and saying there was no surgery. On Wednesday, Glenn opened his news conference by saying he wanted to provide "some clarity" on the injury.

"So he did have a small procedure on his hand," Glenn said. "But the good thing is, man, he's moving his fingers around really, really well."

Glenn said Mitchell waited about a week to 10 days before opting for surgery because he wanted "to see how he progressed and then wanted to go ahead and get it knocked out."

Mitchell has remained on the 53-man roster. The Jets could've put him on IR when the injury occurred, which would've created a roster spot for another player. He had nine receptions for 122 yards in the first two games. Since then, the Jets' receivers not named Wilson have produced only seven receptions and one touchdown.

The Jets are hopeful that Cooper, one of the team's three first-round draft picks this spring, can contribute immediately. He lasted only five snaps in the opener before injuring his ankle. One of those plays was a dazzling catch-and-run that covered 30 yards.

"Obviously, he's a really good player, but you never want any rookie to actually miss time because the reps are valuable for these guys," Glenn said of Cooper.

It looks as if the Jets will be without running back Breece Hall (quadriceps) for the third straight game. Once again, Hall is listed as week-to-week. He didn't practice Wednesday. New York will continue to lean on Braelon Allen, who rushed for a career-high 116 yards and one touchdown in last Sunday's 17-12 win over the visiting Cleveland Browns.

stories.headline: Liverpool rout LASK Linz with Barcola's first UCL hat trick
stories.summary: Bradley Barcola responded to growing but scrutiny of his performances to score his first Champions League hat trick in Liverpool's 6-3 win over LASK Linz.
stories.body:
Bradley Barcola responded to growing but premature scrutiny of his performances to score his first Champions League hat trick in Liverpool's 6-3 win over LASK Linz in Austria.

On a night when Florian Wirtz, the team's only other fit £100 million-plus player, looked more comfortable than he has done all season, it was winger Barcloa who won this competition for the last two seasons with Paris Saint-Germain who sparkled.

Questions had already started to be asked about the France international, probably more a reflection of the underwhelming start Andoni Iraola's side have made, despite the £123 million summer signing having played just six matches.

The 24-year-old provided the perfect riposte, scoring with either foot in the first half to open his account for the club against poor opponents making their debut among Europe's elite.

A far-post tap-in midway through the second half was the easiest of his three, but by then his confidence was soaring, having missed a trio of chances in the win over Atlético Madrid last month.

On-loan Barcelona defender Ronald Araújo made the important breakthrough with a towering header midway through the first half and 95 seconds later Barcola finally came to the party before doubling his tally before the break.

The sight of diminutive right-back Jeremie Frimpong, another player whose overall contribution as has been criticised, scoring with a 12-yard header just after halftime was probably the most surprising element of the whole night.

There was a significant drop in quality from Sunday's opponents Manchester City to the Austrian League champions, who were the perfect foil for players in need of a confidence boost and Barcola exploited the space he was afforded.

Critics have shown little patience with the Frenchman, who suffered from having been omitted from PSG's preseason due to doubts over his future, but with Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai out injured he needed to step up.

That is something which cannot be levelled at 21-year-old Lewis Koumas, who on his first Champions League start had two goals disallowed for offside before finally finding the net with a well-taken first-time shot.

Iraola made four changes from Sunday with two in defence -- Frimpong and Kostas Tsimikas, who claimed two assists, replacing Virgil van Dijk and Milos Kerkez -- with Araujo moving into the centre, Trey Nyoni coming into midfield and Rio Ngumoha on the right wing.

But the 19 shots Liverpool had in the first half alone was an indicator of how one-sided the game was.

Wirtz had one early attempt saved before picking out Barcola with a clever ball down the channel only for him to be flagged offside after he had taken a shot.

But when Araujo out-jumped Alemao to powerfully head down Tsimikas' corner for his first goal it was followed almost immediately by Ngumoha's threatening attack kept alive by Koumas for Barcola to sweep home a first-time shot.

Ryan Gravenberch hit the inside of the post before Barcola slotted past the goalkeeper from Wirtz's fizzed pass.

Six minutes into the second half Frimpong headed in a Tsimikas cross and although Robert Ljubicic pulled one back Koumas' first Champions League goal made it 6-1.

The less said about the defending for Florian Flecker's two late goals the better, but nothing could take the spotlight away from Barcola.

stories.headline: Ducks rookie dons No. 95, channels Lightning McQueen in NHL debut
stories.summary: After a draft night trip to Disneyland to meet Lightning McQueen, the "Cars" synergy came full circle for the Ducks rookie's NHL debut.
stories.body:
Roger McQueen made his NHL debut for the Anaheim Ducks on Tuesday night. He brought inevitable references to the Pixar classic "Cars" with him.

When McQueen was drafted 10th overall in 2025, the Ducks presented him with a No. 95 jersey -- a reference to the car number of Lightning McQueen, the Owen Wilson-voiced protagonist of the "Cars" movies. After he was selected, the McQueen family went to the 55th floor of The Ritz-Carlton in Los Angeles to board a helicopter and fly to Disneyland in nearby Anaheim, where Roger McQueen met Lightning McQueen.

McQueen got the call Monday night that he would be elevated from the AHL to play for the Ducks.

"I thought he got better in camp as he went along. He was one of those guys that would be pushing for a job," coach Joel Quenneville said of the center. "Roger's got some upside in what could be a really nice career."

On Tuesday night, before the Ducks' home game against Calgary Flames, McQueen took his customary rookie lap to start warmups -- wearing No. 95 and sans helmet -- while the arena speakers blared "Real Gone" by Sheryl Crow. While not a staple of arena rock playlists, it was wholly appropriate here: "Real Gone" is the opening track from the "Cars" soundtrack album and was featured in the film.

McQueen played 11:26 in his NHL debut with no points and a shot on goal. It wasn't a memorable night for the Ducks as they lost to the moribund Flames 4-2 in front of a sellout crowd.

One game down, many more to go for McQueen. When he was drafted, Roger's father Scott McQueen said that the "Cars" connection intensifies the spotlight on the young center as he begins his career.

"I think everybody kind of wants to fly under the radar and you know, and just play," Scott said via the CBC. "He wants to prove himself as a player and not so much, you know, as a Disney character."

stories.headline: Sources: Man United assessing Lisandro Martínez comments
stories.summary: Manchester United bosses are assessing Lisandro Martínez's comments in the aftermath of the 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid before deciding whether to take disciplinary action against the Argentina defender, sources have told ESPN.
stories.body:
Manchester United bosses are assessing Lisandro Martínez's comments in the aftermath of the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid before deciding whether to take disciplinary action against the Argentina defender, sources have told ESPN.

Martínez criticised United director of football Jason Wilcox during a bombshell post-match interview on Tuesday night.

- Ogden: Martínez exposes Man United's harsh reality: Blame lies with top brass, not Carrick

The 28-year-old said he "expected more" from Wilcox during the summer transfer window and that the squad is not strong enough "to be ready for this kind of night."

Sources have told ESPN club bosses discussed Martínez's comments on Wednesday, which was a designated day off for the players.

The squad is due to return to the club's Carrington training base on Thursday with Martínez set to find out whether the club will take any further action.

Wilcox, meanwhile, retains the support of United chiefs, sources have told ESPN.

He arrived at Old Trafford as technical director in April 2024 before making the step up to director of football in December in the aftermath of Dan Ashworth's departure.

Ruben Amorim was sacked as head coach in January after his relationship with Wilcox broke down. It's understood that minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who was key to Wilcox's appointment, is happy with his role within United's hierarchy.

Doncic was listed at 244 pounds prior to the 2025-26 season. That dipped to 230 pounds entering training camp. The difference in physique from his heavier days is obvious.

"The guy worked his butt off all summer staying in shape and actually ran this summer," coach JJ Redick said. "He actually did like sprints and stuff. Came into camp in fantastic shape."

The Lakers were without Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler in the preseason opener. Reaves tweaked his ankle recently, and Kessler jammed a finger on the backboard. Both are listed as day-to-day. Without either, the Lakers still rolled through the Kings. Doncic scored all 21 of his points in a 73-point Lakers first half, resting while the backups finished the job. He made three 3s, four shots in the paint and got to the line for nine free throws.

"For someone who normally plays a ton of live basketball [in the summer], he didn't do as much of that by design," Redick said. "We've seen him literally every day in camp incrementally get more and more in rhythm."

San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan.

He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year."

Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4).

Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games.

A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder, after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Wright

Shead agrees to three-year extension in Toronto
Guard Jamal Shead has agreed to a three-year, $24 million extension with the Toronto Raptors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Shead averaged 6.6 points and 5.6 assists per game last season.

Sept. 30

Nuggets add Nembhard on two-way deal

Guard Ryan Nembhard has agreed to a two-way contract with the Denver Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived.

Sept. 29

Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost.

The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN.

Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal?

On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks.

"Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable."

Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30.

Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice
Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday.

"He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see."

After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries.

He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain.

The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona, who is dealing with a sprained left foot.

Anfernee Simons, who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp.

"Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that."

Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season.

Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise.

"With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right?

"But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

Sept. 28

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade

Jayson Tatum's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate.

That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship.

"The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday. "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years."

Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team
It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch.

The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%.

Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience.

Williamson not where he wants to be
New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player.
"I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be."

Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab

Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery, Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp.

"I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly."

Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon.

It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process.

A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule.

"My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater

Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham

Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals.

Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25.

"I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed."

Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season.

"I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit.

"In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard

Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham

The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move.

Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP

At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season.

"No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said.

"The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row.

"We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward."

ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic. No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes

Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling
Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title:

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is."

Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures"

Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year"

During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season.

"The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder."

Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers. The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right."

Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer

Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer.

For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key.

There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract.

"I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do."

Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks

Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons"

At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense."

"I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said.

After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal.

Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset.

"This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win.

"We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi

MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes
The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon.

"It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit.

"My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood."

As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon

Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles

The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season.

Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year"

Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day.

"I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me."

Curry said knee is ready to go for the season

Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee.

"Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with."

Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions.

Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise

Members of the Denver Nuggets' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason.

"We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns."

LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks
New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title.

"I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played.

"I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it."

James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20.

No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation

Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr.'s contract.

"I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that."

The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason.

Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant
Portland Trail Blazers' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday.

"Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player.

"I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent."

Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant.

Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton"

Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season.

"He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need.

"Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks."

Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season.

Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team
Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey.

"It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there."

Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss
After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season.

"I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said.

Harper addresses role for coming season
After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season.

"Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in."

First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team:

"Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language."

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell

stories.headline: MLB changes ALCS Game 3 start time to 1 p.m. due to inclement Cleveland weather
stories.summary: The start time for Game 3 of the ALCS on Thursday was moved up five hours to 1 p.m. ET due to expected inclement weather.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- The start time for Game 3 of the American League Championship Series on Thursday was moved up five hours to 1 p.m. ET because of expected inclement weather.

Major League Baseball announced the changed scheduled time of the game, which was originally scheduled to start at 6 p.m. ET, on Wednesday.

The Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians were off Wednesday after opening the series with two games at Tropicana Field, an enclosed ballpark not subject to the elements. Rain is in the forecast for northeast Ohio on Thursday night as the series transitions to Cleveland's open-air Progressive Field.

The series is tied at one game apiece after the Guardians took Game 1 on Monday and the Rays rebounded to win Game 2 on Tuesday. They are scheduled to play Games 3, 4 and 5 at Progressive Field over three consecutive days through Saturday.

"The change, which is based on forecasted rain on Thursday night in Cleveland, is being made proactively in order to remain on schedule in the ALCS," MLB said in a statement.

The teams would return to Tropicana Field to play Games 6 and 7, if necessary, after a scheduled off-day Sunday.

stories.headline: First-round Phantom Draft: An early look at who goes where, when bids will come
stories.summary: The AFL trade period is over and attention turns to the draft. So who goes where? When will bids land? Here's Jasper Chellappah's early, first-round Phantom Draft.
stories.body:
It's finally draft season.

Changes to draft points and matching bids make for complications on the four club-tied prospects in this Phantom Draft, but they also shorten the first round to 18 selections.

It's a hotly-contested race to be the first overall pick in the open draft. Midfielder Ethan Drever and goalkicker Arki Butler have inside track to be that choice for Essendon, but the decision is still to be narrowed down with Heath Mellody, Harry Van Hattum, and Gus Teixeira all making strong cases.

Bidding changes mean clubs may only match with two selections, and a 20% points loading is given to the Brisbane Lions for making the Grand Final whereas Port Adelaide and GWS receive a 10% discount for missing finals.

It means picks are absorbed within the first round to effectively shorten night one of the AFL Draft.

Recruiters love the depth of the crop that has emerged this year, but a real evenness in talent from 15 through 30 will make for volatile slides and rises come November.

Exactly five weeks out from the 2026 AFL Draft, this is ESPN's first-round Phantom Draft.

1. BID - Port Adelaide: Dougie Cochrane

Port Adelaide/South Australia

FWD/MID/DEF, 195cm

Essendon has all but guaranteed Port Adelaide it will be bidding on Cochrane first overall. He's worth the hype; a roaming key forward with midfield ambitions that played the final month of an injury-plagued top-age campaign behind the ball as a designated kicker. Cochrane has been the nominal first choice in this draft for 24 months and Port Adelaide will have no issue matching, and they've left the door open for clubs to come calling for picks seven and 12 in the lead-up to draft night.

Picks used: 7 and 12

2. Essendon: Ethan Drever

GWV Rebels/Vic Country

MID, 188cm

It's still far from a guarantee that Essendon opt for Drever but there's growing buzz around the powerful midfielder. An injury-free season set him up to dominate for club and state alike, with the Ballarat local producing gaudy numbers for the Rebels and Vic Country. He runs hard both ways, uses his legs to drive out of contest and has a penchant for kicking long-running goals. Similarly to 2016 when they selected skipper Andrew McGrath, the Dons don't have a clear no. 1 in the open pool.

In the mix: Arki Butler, Heath Mellody

3. Richmond: Arki Butler

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID/FWD, 182cm

Richmond's decision here will be highly dependent on their intel into West Coast and Melbourne after them. Butler presents as the best on the board and most unlikely to be available at their next selection. He's a match-winner inside forward 50 with aerial strength and tricks at ground level, kicking goals in bunches and pinch-hitting with power through the middle. With a host of tall forwards and midfielders drafted in recent years, Butler fits nicely amongst the young Tigers nucleus but real interest in Harry Van Hattum could see them flip this order.

In the mix: Harry Van Hattum, Ethan Drever

4. BID - Carlton: Cody Walker

Carlton VFL/Vic Country

MID, 184cm

The Blues are banking on a Walker bid arriving after pick two. Picks 13 and 18 (which become 12 and 17 after a Cochrane bid) is enough to match a bid from three onwards with a minor points deficit. If Essendon surprises by reading out Walker's name in the first two the Blues must have contingencies in place so the son-of-a-gun doesn't slip through. Walker is worthy of a bid at two - he plays at breakneck speed with elite acceleration and evasiveness through the midfield, impressing week in, week out for Carlton's VFL side.

The son of Andrew opted to nominate the Blues over academy club Richmond this year which may dissuade the Tigers from making a bid, but this is close to the end of Walker's draft range and West Coast already has history bidding on Blues father-sons.

Picks used: 12 and 17

5. West Coast: Heath Mellody

Claremont/Western Australia

MID/DEF, 184cm

The hometown kid enjoyed the strongest finish to 2026 of any prospect. Mellody claimed the Larke Medal at the national championships, made his WAFL debut and was one of Claremont's best performers up to the grand final. His name sits comfortably amongst the best in the class with his work rate, clean hands and class by foot making him the perfect complement to Harley Reid and Willem Duursma.

In the mix: Arki Butler, Gus Teixeira

6. Melbourne (via Port Adelaide): Mitch Harris

Woodville-West Torrens/South Australia

DEF, 195cm

Melbourne made a deal to move up two spots in the draft, effectively jumping North's selection at the time. That pick now lands with Sydney but it shouldn't impact who the Dees had in mind. Harris is the bolter this year, rising from a likely second round prospect at the start of the season to the consensus best key defender in the pool. He locks down, intercepts and has shown flashes up forward, plus impressed in SANFL finals to finish the season against mature bodies. The Swans will have interest in Harris given their shallow key defensive stocks, but the Dees will kick off his draft range at this point.

In the mix: Harry Van Hattum, Heath Mellody

7. Richmond (via Port Adelaide): Harry Van Hattum

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

RUC/FWD, 205cm

Richmond would be thrilled to see Van Hattum get through to the pick they brought in via Port Adelaide. The big ruck trained with the club over pre-season and he ripped games apart at various stages of 2026. Van Hattum plays with a physical edge, follows up as an extra midfielder and uses the ball beautifully off his favoured right boot. He looms as the perfect replacement for skipper Toby Nankervis, so much so that Van Hattum could even be snapped up by the Tigers with their first selection before Melbourne gets a look in.

In the mix: Gus Teixeira, Mitch Harris

8. BID - GWS: Ethan Matthews

GWS made an early bid on Harry Kyle last year and Sydney can return the favour here. Trading into pick six via the Blakey deal puts the Swans firmly in the range of Matthews, an excellent midfield prospect that racks up the ball and uses it with composure off his left foot. GWS would be matching with pick 11 at this stage, and could look to trade points into future years on the night to maximise their draft hand while still landing their academy gun. Matthews is clearly the best Giants Academy prospect since Tom Green in 2019.

Picks used: 11 and 19

9. Sydney (via North Melbourne): Gus Teixeira

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

MID, 181cm

If the top key defender is off the board the Swans will have an eye on the best available talent, having not drafted a top-10 talent since Logan McDonald and Braeden Campbell in 2020. Teixeira is the highly rated prospect that slides in this phantom, but could easily be snapped up by the Dees or Tigers prior. Playing with powerful drive in the forward half, Teixeira's impact with ball in hand has been a standout all season. He'll start his career as a general forward but there's little doubt amongst recruiters that Teixeira will soon be a midfielder at the next level.

In the mix: Mitch Harris, Tyson Bradley

10. Gold Coast (FA compensation): Sam Gayfer

Northern Knights/Vic Metro

FWD, 194cm

Gayfer is deserving of a top 10 pick this year and the Suns come into this selection through Ben King's departure. Even while bringing in Aidan Schubert their key forward stocks are thin and Gayfer is the competitive beast that Damien Hardwick covets. He crashes packs, pressures at ground level and can jump on heads to take massive marks. The Suns swooping here would be a blow for the Saints and Pies who are keen on the athletic tall.

In the mix: Tyson Bradley, Clancy Snell

11. BID - Brisbane: Caylen Murray

Lions Academy/Allies

DEF/MID, 183cm

The Keidean Coleman trade to Essendon at the death gives Brisbane three picks in the second round that will need to be consolidated to match a bid at this stage. The academy star has some similarities to Coleman in his precise ball use off halfback. He generates run and is safe with ball in hand, making the right decisions and creating space for himself and others. Murray appeals as a replacement for Dayne Zorko and could play significant football in 2027, with the Saints on the lookout for a ball user of his quality.

12. St Kilda: Wil Malady

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

FWD, 190cm

The Saints would love to see Gayfer here as a key forward option, but have a nice group of talls to pick from. Malady is the wildcard play, with excellent athleticism including a big leap and sensational agility at his size. He works himself into the ground as a link between the forwards and midfielders, but can also play deep as a dangerous aerial target.

In the mix: Sam Gayfer, Lochie Burrows

13. Collingwood: Tyson Bradley

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

DEF, 195cm

The Pies are in the market for a tall at either end of the ground and will get one at this spot. Bradley is ultra composed and a steady kick out of defence, twisting and turning out of trouble and relieving pressure for his side. He also competes well in the air against key forwards including successful matchups on Malady and Gayfer in finals contests. Clubs have loved his leadership and character qualities so he could land even higher than this mark. Collingwood will be eager to see if Gayfer gets through as the nephew of premiership defender Mick.

In the mix: Sam Gayfer, Clancy Snell, Wil Malady

14. Melbourne (via Port Adelaide): Leo Steed

Swan Districts/Western Australia

MID, 176cm

If the Dees go tall with Harris or Van Hattum first they can get their midfielder here. Steed is ultra professional, a two-way runner and brings his courage and toughness to every contest. Recruiters are confident the WA hard nut makes it as an on-baller at the next level and Melbourne is primed to add youth to that area of the ground.

In the mix: Toby Krasna, Jake Eime

15. Adelaide: Clancy Snell

Gippsland Power/Vic Country

DEF, 196cm

The Crows held onto Nick Murray but lost Jordon Butts and are thin down back. Snell gives them a high-upside swing at the best intercept defender in the class. He's an elite aerialist that backs himself to kickstart transition. They remain in need of some dash out of defence with local product Jake Eime's range beginning at this point too.

In the mix: Tyson Bradley, Jake Eime, Kodah Edwards

16. St Kilda (via Geelong): Lochie Burrows

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

DEF/MID, 181cm

The Saints are keen on Burrows. A local Bentleigh product whose best trait may be his versatility, Burrows has been thrown around the ground and excelled everywhere. He can get his hands dirty as a contested midfielder, lock down and offer dash out of defence and worked hard on his forward craft over pre-season with an eye to a role off half forward. If the Saints sniff out interest in Burrows around this mark they could even snap up the high-character talent with their first selection.

In the mix: Leo Steed, Jackson Phillips, Jake Eime

17. Essendon (via Hawthorn): George Dimer

Sandringham Dragons/Vic Metro

FWD, 173cm

Dimer earns big plaudits from clubs for his character and selfless nature. As a small forward he has the speed to separate and the nous to sniff out the goals but also plays with a team-first attitude that sees him set up a lot of scores. He played midfield in his juniors and brings his ball-winning to the forward half. Small forward is a huge area of need for the Dons but there will also be a host of clubs keen on Dimer from this stage on.

In the mix: Clancy Snell, Jack Pickett, Toby Krasna

18. Fremantle: Jake Soutar

East Perth

DEF, 190cm

The Dockers are entrenched in their premiership window and Soutar would have played significant football at a lot of clubs towards the end of 2026. The 20-year-old was East Perth's fairest and best after a breakout season in the WAFL, intercepting and creating off halfback including a big finals campaign. He's a good size to play on various forwards and has the body to compete for Luke Ryan's role straight away. A mature-ager is a bold selection in the first round but Soutar is a win-now pick in a role Fremantle needs to address.

In the mix: Leo Steed, Toby Krasna

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Max Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant drive at Singapore GP

- Lewis Hamilton calls Singapore GP strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: The UFC's flyweights are hot again - is Lone'er Kavanagh the next star?
stories.summary: Could a breakout win at UFC 333 propel Britain's Lone'er Kavanagh into the flyweight title picture?
stories.body:
The fighting life of a UFC flyweight was once an unenvied one.

Constant uncertainty over the future of the division, a lack of big pay-per-view interest and an unfortunate routine of far too many fighters getting cut for the weight class to sustain itself were just some of the problems that characterised the modern era. UFC president Dana White put it in simple terms, saying after Demetrious Johnson's UFC exit in 2018 that "people didn't care" about the flyweights. Even Olympic gold medalist and former two-division champion Henry Cejudo struggled to see how the flyweight division would continue as a part of the UFC, with his own brash persona and entertaining title defences pivotal to maintaining awareness of the division.

Much has changed since the days of Cejudo though, and the flyweights now have a genuine claim to being one of the most exciting divisions in the whole of the UFC. And one man at the forefront of that charge is another promising fighting talent from across the Atlantic, with England's Lone'er Kavanagh enjoying a rise like few others this past year.

He accepted a short-notice fight against ex-champion Brandon Moreno in the lion's den of Mexico City in March and produced one of the most stunning UFC upsets in recent memory, taking the unanimous decision win in front of a hostile crowd. Kavanagh was unranked before that fight and despite more recently losing to Brandon Royval at UFC 329, he remains just a win away from breaking into the flyweight title conversation. Taking on Royval on the night of Conor McGregor's return in Las Vegas in July, Kavanagh was submitted but earned the fight of the night on one of the promotion's most-watched recent cards in a back-and-forth slugfest. The 27-year-old's exciting style and high ceiling was on show that evening and will be again when he faces Ramazonbek Temirov on what is remarkably just his second high-profile numbered event at UFC 333 on Oct. 24.

"Thinking back to certain moments [in Mexico City], it was like a rollercoaster, it was a sick opportunity and I'm glad I did it and my team backed me to do it," Kavanagh tells ESPN.

"[Royval was] another step on the journey, losing is never fun, no matter what stage you're at whether you're at the top or at any point of your career but unfortunately sometimes you have to learn like that -- learning on the go, that's what we're doing right now.

"I believe I've got the best team around me so I truly believe with this team I can make it all the way to the top and that's the plan, that's the aim.

"I'm always trying to work on things from every fight. Unfortunately, you learn a lot more when you lose."

For Kavanagh, the lights have quickly turned brighter. Like many of his British counterparts in the UFC, he was made in Cage Warriors, the organisation that can take credit for the likes of McGregor, Paddy Pimblett and Tom Aspinall. From there, a first round knockout on Dana White's Contender Series saw the journey in the big time begin. His first professional defeat came in the UFC against the experienced Charles Johnson, but that was quickly forgotten with the Moreno heist that saw his stock in the game skyrocket. Kavanagh's front-footed, devious style stemming from his kickboxing roots has even earned him praise from one of the greatest to ever step in the octagon with a Jon Jones Facetime after that UFC Mexico win leaving him "starstruck."

"Your Muay Thai is beautiful, your kicks, they don't show at all. They have no telegraph. It's so nice," Jones said to Kavanagh.

It is a style that was born at London's Great Britain Top Team (GBTT), where alongside UFC veteran Nathaniel Wood and fellow prospect Shanelle Dyer, Kavanagh has honed his craft, going from a five-time K1 kickboxing champion to now potentially a statement win away from challenging for UFC gold under British MMA trailblazer Brad Pickett. And that too in a division where the competition is possibly as fierce as it has ever been. Royval, Tatsuro Tairo, Manuel Kape, Asu Almabayev and bona fide flyweight royalty Alexandre Pantoja make up the spine of a group of challengers that Kananagh finds himself a part of.

Joshua Van's UFC 331 title defence ended any doubts about his validity as champion, with a dominant win over Pantoja, and at just 24-years-old he looks set for a stint at the top -- where Kavanagh aspires to be. But first, No. 7 ranked, one below Kavanagh, and unbeaten in the UFC, the explosive Temirov is one of the toughest challenges the Englishman has faced in his career, and in a weight class as deep as the flyweights, back-to-back losses would see Kavanagh fall mercilessly down the pecking order -- the stakes are high at UFC 333.

"I think the flyweight division is the best division at the moment. It's forever changing," Kavanagh says. "There are so many young up and comers but there are also so many people that have been around for so long. So it's got a good mixture of everything and to be honest, just excited to be a part of it - it's sick being a flyweight at this time.

"I'm a very 'one fight at a time' kind of person, I'll always look at what's in front of me and then what's next but I think it would be an exciting fight either way, [Joshua] Van vs. Lon."

Born in London to an Irish father and Chinese mother, Kavanagh wears his heritage on his sleeve with his name Lone'er translating to "Little Dragon" in English. He credits his mum for pushing him into MMA, a decision that has since paid dividends.

Kavanagh is now set to be a part of a main card alongside two title fights at the Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. In his way, Uzbekistan's Temirov is coming in red hot on the back of a first-round finish against Steve Erceg, he last tasted defeat in an MMA bout seven years ago and has never been knocked out.

"I haven't seen all the fighters just fighting like me. Just striking punches, just making knockouts. But my punches will just kill them all," Temirov told the UFC.

The kickboxer is aware of the danger that Temirov carries but also the opportunity up for grabs.

"I think a win there puts me right back up there. He's a dangerous opponent. He's got some good wins under him, a lot of wins, but I think a win against him puts me right back up at the top. [I'm] always looking for a finish," Kavanagh said.

"His main weapons are his heavy hands, and that excites me. I love fights like that and I think it's a good fight for me. Hopefully [another fight of the night], I'm looking for more performances of the night."

As is now customary with Kavanagh's UFC bouts, his throwdown against the formidable Temirov is one not to be missed. With the top of the flyweight division so deep he will want to turn all the excitement surrounding him into consistency to earn a shot at Van's belt, that journey will take its latest step in a treacherous division.

And as Bruce Buffer introduces both fighters, perhaps there will be something for the UFC bosses and fans alike to take away before a single punch is even thrown. That all these years after Cejudo and Johnson have been and gone, the flyweights are box office property once again.

stories.headline: Dream's Gray has minor procedure on hand ahead of Finals opener
stories.summary: Allisha Gray, who has missed the Dream's past two playoff games because of a left hand injury, is still day-to-day heading into the WNBA Finals after undergoing a minor procedure.
stories.body:
Four-time All-Star Allisha Gray underwent a minor procedure on her left hand and is still considered day-to-day for the Atlanta Dream heading into the WNBA Finals, she said Tuesday.

"Progress is great," Gray told WSB-TV when asked at practice whether she'd play in Game 1. "As of right now just day-to-day, and you'll see."

Gray did not clarify whether she had surgery on her hand, and the team declined to say when the procedure occurred.

She was seen taking shots at practice Tuesday, a day before the team travels to the Bay Area for Saturday's Finals opener against No. 2 seed Golden State.

Gray, the top scorer for the No. 4 seed Dream, has missed the past two playoff games after injuring the hand in the first half of Game 1 in a semifinal series against the New York Liberty. She was listed as questionable heading into Game 3 last Friday against New York and went through warmups before being ruled out "in the interest of caution," according to coach Karl Smesko.

The Dream advanced to the Finals with a three-game sweep.

Gray, a 6-foot guard out of South Carolina, averaged 19.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.4 steals this year while appearing in all 44 regular-season games. She was also the Dream's top scorer (22.0 points per game) during their first-round sweep of the No. 5 seed Washington Mystics.

The Dream and Valkyries will both be competing for their first WNBA championship.

stories.headline: Garber won't dish on exchange with Messi: 'Between me and Leo'
stories.summary: Don Garber has addressed his September confrontation with Lionel Messi, and the MLS commissioner said he admired the exchange.
stories.body:
Don Garber has addressed his confrontation with Lionel Messi following Inter Miami CF Campeones Cup victory over Cruz Azul in September, with the MLS commissioner saying he admired the exchange.

Following the Campeones Cup victory, Messi and Garber could be seen having a heated discussion before the Inter Miami captain went to celebrate the victory with the rest of his team and family members.

"You know, the best players in the world have passion," Garber said in an interview with Front Office Sports on Tuesday. "The legendary players have more than passion. Leo played on Saturday, scored a couple goals and assists coming out of an international window where he played for Argentina, 39 years old. He's leading our rush for Golden Boot. He's leading our MVP race.

"There are players throughout history, Muhammad Ali, Wayne Gretzky, Michael Jordan who play with a sense of intensity and passion that makes them unique and special, and makes him the GOAT of all GOATS. What is going on there is between me and Leo [Messi], it's not something I am going to talk about with you.

"But I admire it, I appreciate it and I think it's what makes Leo Messi the greatest player ever to play football. And I will say, [he's] the greatest athlete of all time."

Inter Miami beat Cruz Azul 2-0 in the Campeones Cup final with a goal from Messi in the 24th minute before he provided the assist to Casemiro for the second goal. Messi currently has 23 goals and 13 assists in MLS, leading the 2026 Golden Boot race and sitting in second place for most assists so far this regular season.

It's not the first time that Garber and Messi haven't seen eye to eye. In 2025, Garber made a joke about Messi not wanting to talk to him following the decision to suspend him and former teammate Jordi Alba for missing the 2025 MLS All-Star Game.

"I don't think he wants to talk to me," Garber said in 2025. "I didn't treat him like any other player in that decision. So, I probably won't be going to Miami any time soon or hanging out and doing any media work with Leo."

Garber later defended his decision to suspend the two players.

"If you don't do that, you're not gonna be able to lead," Garber said. "You're not gonna be able to command the respect of the ownership. The media is going to s--- on you no matter what. You guys will write a story 'how could you suspend Leo Messi?' after we suspended him, and before we suspended him say 'how could you not?'

"So, the media is irrelevant to that equation. They're gonna hate you all the time."

Garber and Messi later interacted at the 2025 MLS Cup, when the MLS commissioner presented the Inter Miami captain with the trophy. Inter Miami currently sits second place on the Eastern Conference table with 49 points from 28 games.

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."

stories.headline: What we've learned about the Detroit Lions after five weeks
stories.summary: At 3-2, Detroit enters its bye having found some much-needed momentum in Arizona. Here is a closer look.
stories.body:
DETROIT -- A smiling Derrick Barnes was among the final Detroit Lions players to leave visitor's locker room at State Farm Stadium on Sunday.

Fresh off a 45-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals, the linebacker admitted it "felt good" to enter Detroit's Week 6 bye on a high note -- especially after the team's defensive struggles early in the season.

"I'm ready to get back to it. Out there, that's us. That's who we are," Barnes said. "Obviously, we have to continue to do it week in and week out but going out there and proving ourselves right today and then having the bye week. I said, 'I'm ready to get back to football already.' That's who we can be. It's a beautiful thing."

Throughout the week, Barnes said he had received several text messages from Dan Campbell in which Detroit's head coach expressed his urgency to win and to go "whip ass" in Arizona.

The Lions entered the Cardinals game allowing a league-worst 31.8 points per game, which was their highest mark allowed through four games of a season since 2022 when they allowed 35.3 points, per ESPN Research.

But after giving up a touchdown on the Cardinals' opening drive, the defense adjusted. The Cards scored a late touchdown when the game had already been decided. 

Campbell was fired up after the win, but also challenged his coaching staff to do a deep dive to find out "who are we really?"

"I think we're five [games] in now and we've continued to evolve a little bit and we're mixing some things up," Campbell said on Monday. "But, at this point now we need to figure out what we really are and what we do well."

At 3-2, Detroit enters its bye having found some much-needed momentum in Arizona. Here is a closer look at what we've learned about the Lions so far.

What have we learned about the Lions on offense?

Under new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, the Lions are averaging 32.8 points per game, which is tied with the Buffalo Bills for the most in the NFL. It's the second-most points they've scored through five games in franchise history, behind only last season (34.8 per game), but Campbell still feels they can get off to faster starts, involve wide receiver Jameson Williams more consistently, create a stronger ground attack and become more dominant as a unit overall.

Lions quarterback Jared Goff has emerged as an early MVP candidate, throwing for 1,485 yards (second-most in the league) with 12 touchdowns and zero interceptions. Star running back Jahmyr Gibbs came out of Week 5 fourth in the league with 504 rushing yards and first in scrimmage touchdowns (nine) in his new role as the predominant back, but the standards are high in Detroit.

"I think the sentiment is we have been good," Goff said after practice last week. "We've done some good things, and we've scored and had some good drives, but we haven't been great. And we're very, very capable of being great and above that. We want to be the best offense in the league, and we have to start playing like it."

What have we learned about the Lions on defense?

Defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard was under fire after his unit gave up at least 30 points in three of the first four games. But the unit put up a solid performance in Arizona entering the off week. The secondary has struggled the most, allowing a league-high 1,487 passing yards through the first five games. The defensive line, however, has produced the most sacks (20) through the first five games of any season in franchise history.

Four players have at least three sacks, with edge DJ Wonnum leading the team with 5.0, followed by Aidan Hutchinson (4.0), DL Alim McNeill (3.5) and Barnes (3.0). Against Arizona, the defense committed to more man coverage which seemed to help, but also may not be the long-term the answer.

"You have to go by what opponent it is," Campbell said.

What do we still need to see from the Lions on offense?

Faster starts. Despite ending with 45 points, Detroit's offense went three-and-out on the first three drives in Arizona before scoring on its next seven.

Detroit has scored one touchdown on 13 drives that have ended in the first quarter this season (7.7%) after scoring a touchdown on 24% of their first-quarter drives last season, which tied for ninth highest in the NFL, per ESPN Research.

Goff would like to improve in that area.

"It felt like (Petzing) could call whatever he wanted and we were going to make it work," Goff said after the Cardinals win. "I think today was a good example of, like I've said, where we can go and what we are capable of. I think I said it earlier last week (but) we've been good, right? Today we were great, and there are still some things to be better at certainly, but today we were like 'OK, that's what we were capable of.' It's good to know that's our standard now and we can hold guys accountable to what we just did today."

What do we still need to see from the Lions on defense?
Improvement in the secondary. Moving forward, the Lions are anticipating the return of Pro Bowl defensive back Brian Branch, who has been sidelined since December 2025 with a torn Achilles. They were also engaged in trade talks for Joey Porter Jr., who ultimately ended up in Dallas, as part of their search to find another cornerback. ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler has suggested that Kansas City's Kristian Fulton and Pittsburgh's Jalen Ramsey could be potential targets.

Branch, who started the season on the PUP list, had his 21-day practice window opened on Oct. 7. Campbell said he won't rush Branch back on the field, but he's very close to returning.

"I told Dan, I'm starving since I got injured. Just been day by day. Just been working, just been grinding. Showing up at 7 a.m.," Branch said last week.

Branch said he's "getting the rust off now in practice. I feel good."

"I'm ready to go," Branch said.

The Lions' depleted secondary also entered the season without Pro Bowl safety Kerby Joseph and is missing safety Thomas Harper and defensive back Avonte Maddox, who are on injured reserve.
